bib.title: Agent S: An Open Agentic Framework that Uses Computers Like a Human

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Agent S: An Open Agentic Framework That Uses Computers Like a Human", Saaket Agashe, Jiuzhou Han, Shuyu Gan, Jiachen Yang, Ang Li, Xin Eric Wang (Simular Research). Preprint, arXiv:2410.08164v1, 10 Oct 2024.

COVERAGE: All 23 of 23 pages read. That is all 70,613 of 70,613 chars, including appendices A-D. I skimmed the reference list for origins. The extraction is clean text. Figures are image-only, so the figure contents are not extracted. I did not read the target note in full, only grepped it. It currently covers MemGPT/Letta (Packer et al. 2023), with no Agent S material.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Agent S roughly doubles the best OSWorld baseline.
  number: 20.58% vs 11.21% (GPT-4o), +9.37 points, 83.6% relative.
  setup: OSWorld full test set, 369 Ubuntu tasks, GPT-4o backbone, screenshot plus accessibility tree input.
  quote: "Agent S achieves an overall success rate of 20.58%, nearly doubling the performance of the best corresponding baseline (GPT-4o with 11.21%)."
  where: p.7, Sec 4.2; Table 1 p.8.
- Removing experience retrieval costs the most when it is web knowledge, and removing all three sources roughly halves the score.
  number: Agent S 26.15 overall. Without web knowledge 16.80, without narrative memory 21.41, without episodic memory 18.46, without all 13.85.
  setup: testsub, a 65-task stratified subset of OSWorld, GPT-4o. The subset is small (OS has 6 tasks, Professional 10). The authors say they chose it for inference cost.
  quote: "- w/o Web Knowledge 16.60 11.76 24.49 30.00 6.25 16.80 / - w/o Narrative Memory 33.33 11.76 36.99 20.00 12.50 21.41 / - w/o Episodic Memory 33.33 5.88 25.00 30.00 12.50 18.46 / - w/o All 33.33 5.88 18.75 20.00 6.25 13.85"
  where: p.9, Table 2.
  Note: of the two memory types, dropping episodic memory costs more (about 7.7 points) than dropping narrative (about 4.7).
- Storing a self-evaluated summary beats storing raw trajectories. Self-supervised exploration matters most for building memory.
  number: Agent S 26.15. Without self-evaluator 18.46, without exploration 15.38, without continual update 23.08 (Table 7). Figure 7 prints 23.18 for the same ablation.
  setup: testsub, 65 tasks, GPT-4o. "w/o Self-Evaluator" replaces summaries with full trajectories.
  quote: "Agent S - w/o Exploration 15.38% / Agent S - w/o Self-Evaluator 18.46% / Agent S - w/o Continual Memory Update 23.18% / Agent S 26.15%"
  where: p.9, Figure 7; Appendix A.3 Table 7, p.15.
- Retrieval helps much more once the ACI and hierarchical planning are present.
  number: Baseline 10.77 goes to 12.31 with retrieval. Agent S ACI-only is 12.31, 20.00 with retrieval, 26.15 full.
  setup: testsub, GPT-4o. The "ACI-only + retrieval" setup excludes hierarchical planning.
  quote: "Agent S 26.15% / Agent S (ACI + Retrieval) 20.00% / Agent S (ACI-only) 12.31% / Baseline + Retrieval 12.31% / Baseline 10.77%"
  where: p.9, Figure 6; Table 6 p.15.
- Memory design is two-level.
  number: none.
  setup: Narrative memory (Manager) stores abstractive summaries of whole-task trajectories, successful and failed, with specific actions removed, keyed by the query Q. Episodic memory (Worker) stores successful subtask strategies with grounded actions, keyed by <task, subtask, context>. Retrieval is by embedding similarity (text-embedding-3-small). The Self-Evaluator writes these without human feedback or ground truth.
  quote: "Narrative Memory includes summaries of both successful and failed trajectories with specific actions removed as abstractive full task experience" and "Episodic Memory includes a complete plan with specific grounding actions and only summaries from the subtask trajectories designated as DONE or successful by a Worker."
  where: p.4-5, Sec 3.1.
- Memory is bootstrapped by self-supervised exploration, then updated continually at inference time.
  number: top 50 common tasks per application, plus environment-aware generated tasks.
  setup: exploration runs use web knowledge only. After that, memory is updated on each inference task.
  quote: "we leverage a task generator to generate the top 50 most common tasks from the various applications used in OSWorld"
  where: p.5-6, Sec 3.2.
- Learning here is retrieval, not weight updates. The authors compare the loop to hierarchical RL.
  number: none.
  quote: "mirrors a classic Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning process - but uses Retrieval as a learning strategy."
  where: p.5, Sec 3.1.3.
- Two modules are introduced beyond memory. The Trajectory Reflector gives the Worker advice to avoid repeated actions. The Experience Context Fusion step merges web knowledge with the retrieved narrative memory into one guideline.
  number: none.
  where: p.4-5.
- It generalises to Windows with no adaptation.
  number: 18.2% vs 13.3% (NAVI).
  setup: WindowsAgentArena, all 154 tasks, GPT-4o, accessibility tree plus image. The baseline's best agent uses an internal model that is not accessible, so the comparison is against a similar configuration. Agent S scores 0.0 in Office and 13.3 in Web Browser against NAVI's 20.0.
  quote: "Agent S 0.0 13.3 45.8 29.2 19.1 22.2 18.2"
  where: p.10, Table 4.
- Most failures are execution and grounding errors.
  number: of failed testsub tasks, Execution Error 79.59%, Grounding 53.06%, Planning 34.69%, Subtask Failure 57.17%. Of 39 execution errors, 46% were caused by planning or grounding, and 54% were self-induced.
  setup: failed tasks only. One task can have several errors.
  quote: "Planning Error 66.67 25.00 30.00 66.67 28.57 34.69 / Grounding Error 0.00 75.00 50.00 66.67 35.71 53.06 / Execution Error 33.33 87.50 100.00 66.67 71.43 79.59"
  where: p.10, Table 3; p.21, Fig 13.
- The ACI bounds the action space to one discrete primitive per step.
  number: 11 primitives in Table 5 (click, type, scroll, hotkey, hold_and_press, drag_and_drop, save_to_buffer, switch_applications, wait, done, fail). Elements are referenced by integer tags in the accessibility tree, which is augmented with OCR text blocks matched by IOU.
  where: p.6-7, Sec 3.3; p.15.

LIMITS
- The authors concede they did not measure steps or wall-clock time, and call for Pareto analysis of time against accuracy ("A key metric that has been unaddressed... is the number of agent steps and wall clock time").
- Open-source and smaller models are untested. Only GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet were used.
- Ablations use 65 tasks on GPT-4o only, so single-point differences are noisy. The full-test-set comparison has no variance or seeds reported.
- There is no analysis of memory growth, staleness, retrieval failures or contamination. Exploration tasks are generated from the OSWorld and WindowsArena initial environments, so there may be overlap with the test environments. The paper does not discuss this.
- The domain is GUI desktop control, so transfer of the memory design to chat or text agents is not shown.
- Dated: the results are Oct 2024, and the baselines are 2024-era models.

BUILDS ON (as printed): Sumers et al. 2024 (cognitive architectures for language agents); Shinn et al. 2023 (Reflexion); Park et al. 2023 (Generative Agents); Yang et al. 2024 (the SWE-agent ACI) and Lieberman & Selker 2003 (the ACI concept); Xie et al. 2024 (OSWorld); Bonatti et al. 2024 (WindowsAgentArena); Kagaya et al. 2024 (RAP); Fu et al. 2024 (AutoGuide); Kim et al. 2024 (RADA); Wei et al. 2022 and Yao et al. 2023 (chain-of-thought and ReAct style templated reasoning). MemGPT is not cited in the extracted text.

CODE: no code listings. The formulas are the load-bearing items, in Sec 3.1.1 and Appendix C, p.17:
"Q = LLM(Tu, O0)
Kweb = Retrieve(Web, Q)
Enu = Retrieve(Mn, Q)
Kfused = LLM(Mn(Q), Kweb)"
and "Esi = Retrieve(Me, ⟨Tu, si, Csi ⟩)".

FIGURES
- Fig 1, p.1: system overview showing the memory flow. Web search plus narrative memory feed planning, and episodic memory feeds subtask execution.
- Fig 3, p.4: Manager and Worker with Narrative and Episodic memory, the Self-Evaluator write-back loop, and the ACI. Best single picture of the architecture.
- Fig 4, p.6: exploration, then continual memory update pipeline.
- Fig 6 and Fig 7, p.9: ablation bars (ACI and memory update).
- Fig 2, p.2: per-category comparison against the OSWorld agent. Fig 13, p.21: execution error sources.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions found.
- Minor internal inconsistencies:
  - Fig 7 gives 23.18 and Table 7 gives 23.08 for "w/o Continual Memory Update".
  - Table 2 "w/o Web Knowledge" overall (16.80) does not match the per-column values (16.60 for OS).
  - The setup text says "Claude-3-Sonnet" while Table 1 says Claude-3.5.
  - The per-domain Table 8 baseline row differs from Table 1.
  - Appendix D.1 success examples are images only.
- The paper's memory is task-experience retrieval (RAG-style), not an OS-style context-paging design like MemGPT. It is a contrast case for note 03, not a direct extension.
